title: Karl Organizing: Benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Benefit Events] Can you explain: we want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Here's the thing: Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause.

title: Karl Organizing: Neighborhood Pods
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Neighborhood Pods] A friend asked me: 'How many houses should be in one neighborhood pod to keep it manageable?' What do I tell them?

Keep it tight—ten to fifteen households is the sweet spot for actually knowing your neighbors' names and needs. If it gets too big, communication breaks down and people start feeling like a number again. You want a group where one person can walk to everyone else's front door in five minutes if the internet goes down. Once you hit twenty houses, it's time to split and help the next block start their own pod.

title: Karl Organizing: Building a Platform
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building a Platform] A friend asked me: 'What should be at the top of my local campaign platform?' What do I tell them?

Housing as a human right, period. If you aren't talking about rent control, social housing, and an end to homelessness, you aren't serious about helping the working class. Add in a demand for robust public transit and a promise to tax the big local businesses to pay for it all. Keep the language simple and the promises bold so the average person knows exactly whose side you are on from the jump.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Fridge Startup] How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Here's how it works: Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Lease Renewals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Lease Renewals] Our leases are up soon and the landlord wants to hike the rent by 20%. What now?

Refuse to sign as individuals. Form a bargaining committee and tell the landlord that nobody signs a new lease until the hike is capped at a reasonable rate for everyone. You have more leverage when 40 units are at stake instead of one. If they want that guaranteed income, they have to negotiate with the union like any other business partner.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Pooling] How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Here's the thing: Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

Here's the thing: A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] Can you explain: how do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sustaining the Fight
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sustaining the Fight] How do we keep people from burning out on rapid response?

Here's how it works: Rotate your shifts and make sure nobody is on call 24/7 or they'll be useless within a month. Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and make time for communal meals and joy that have nothing to do with the pigs. This is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need every comrade healthy and sharp for the long haul. Rest is a radical act when the state wants you exhausted.

title: Karl Organizing: Mutual aid vs charity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mutual aid vs charity] What's the difference between mutual aid and charity?

Charity flows one way — from the haves to the have-nots, with strings and savior complexes attached. Mutual aid flows in circles: today you stock the fridge, tomorrow you eat from it. No means testing, no moral judgment, no nonprofit industrial complex taking a cut. Solidarity, not pity.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: decision Making] Give me the short version: How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Let me break it down: Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot.

title: Karl Organizing: Social pressure
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social pressure] How do we handle coworkers who are openly against the union?

Don't waste all your energy on the hardcore 'no' votes. Focus on the 'undecideds' and the 'soft yes' folks. For the ones who are actively sabotaging, let their own friends and coworkers talk to them. Social pressure from peers is way more effective than any argument you can make. If they want to be the boss's pet, let them explain that to the people they work with every day. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Real talk: Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, disability Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, disability Accessibility] How do we make our mutual aid events more accessible for disabled comrades?

Here's the thing: Start by asking disabled folks what they need instead of guessing and getting it wrong. Ensure every meeting spot has ramps and sensory-friendly spaces, and always provide captions or ASL if you're doing a presentation. Mutual aid that ignores the most marginalized among us isn't mutual—it's just a club for the able-bodied. Build accessibility into the foundation of your group so no one has to 'request' entry to their own community.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building Trust] How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Here's the thing: Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, safe Zones] How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Real talk: Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: Retaliation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Retaliation] What if they fire me for organizing?

Here's the thing: It's illegal, but it happens because bosses are criminals. That's why we organize in teams. If they fire a leader, the whole shop needs to be ready to walk out or take action immediately. We protect each other. We file charges with the NLRB, but we also make the boss's life a living hell through public pressure and direct action until you're back on the job.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, security Culture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, security Culture] How do we keep our coalition safe from people trying to break us up?

Keep your sensitive planning to small, vetted groups and leave the public posturing for the rallies. Don't talk about illegal tactics on apps that the cops can read, and verify the identity of anyone who wants access to your data or money. Paranoia is a trap, but being smart about who knows what is just basic survival in a fight against people with infinite resources. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Real talk: Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way.

title: Karl Organizing: Captive audience meetings
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Captive audience meetings] Do I have to go to the company's anti-union meetings?

Let me break it down: If they're mandatory, go, but don't go alone. Walk in as a group, sit together, and take notes on every lie they tell. If you've got the numbers, have everyone wear union shirts or buttons. Better yet, have a few respected workers ask tough questions that the suits can't answer. Turn their propaganda session into a demonstration of your collective strength.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, volunteer Management] How do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, public Messaging] How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response Setup] A friend asked me: 'How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?' What do I tell them?

Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. title: Karl Organizing: Metadata Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Metadata Awareness] Can you explain: what is 'scrubbing' and how do I do it?

Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Interrogation Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Interrogation Tactics] What if the detective is being nice and says they just want to help me?

The 'good cop' is a myth designed to get you to snitch on your friends. They will lie about what your comrades said and offer you fake deals to get you talking. Don't fall for it. The only thing you say in that room is 'I want my lawyer' and then you stare at the wall until they bring one. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: childcare Collectives] Give me the short version: How can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?

Look, Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, childcare Collectives

text:

title: Karl Organizing: Security Deposits
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security Deposits] My old landlord is refusing to give back my deposit for no reason. How do I get it?

Send a formal demand letter via certified mail citing the specific state law they're breaking. In many places, if they don't return it or provide an itemized list of repairs within 30 days, they owe you double or triple the amount. Tell them you'll see them in small claims court and that you're bringing your tenant union to testify about their pattern of theft.

title: Karl Organizing: Grassroots fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grassroots fundraising] How do we fundraise without corporate donors?

Here's how it works: Small-dollar, high-volume: monthly sustainers at $5-25, benefit shows, merch that people actually want to wear, community dinners. Be radically transparent about where money goes — publish the budget. And never take money that comes with strings. A $10,000 corporate donation that silences your demands is a loss, not a win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: enemy Propaganda] Give me the short version: The local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?

Look, Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] Can you explain: how do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: crowd Logistics] Give me the short version: How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: Security Culture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Paranoia is a trap, but being smart about who knows what is just basic survival in a fight against people with infinite resources. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Fund Priorities
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Fund Priorities] Our bail fund is small. How do we decide who to get out of jail first?

Prioritize the comrades most at risk: trans folks, people with urgent medical needs, and parents who might lose their kids if they miss a day of work. We aren't here to play judge or jury; we're here to snatch our neighbors back from the state's kidnapping machine. Get those who are facing the longest pre-trial stretches out first so they can fight their cases from a position of strength. Every person we free is a middle finger to the carceral state.

title: Karl Organizing: Escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Escalation Management] What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed.

title: Karl Organizing: Stop and Identify
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Stop and Identify] Do I have to show my ID if an officer stops me on the street?

In most places, you only have to show ID if they have a 'reasonable suspicion' you've committed a crime, but it's safer to ask 'Am I free to go?' If they say yes, walk away. If they say no, you're being detained; give them your name and birthdate if your local laws require it, then shut up and wait for a lawyer.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: benefit Events
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: benefit Events] Give me the short version: We want to host a fundraiser but don't have a budget for a venue. What do we do?

Find a comrade with a backyard or a local dive bar that hates the status quo as much as we do. Throw a rent party with local bands or a radical trivia night where the entry fee goes straight into the war chest. You don't need a ballroom when you have a community willing to pack into a basement for the cause.

title: Karl Organizing: Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accessibility] How do we make sure disabled comrades can join the protest safely?

You can't call it a mass movement if you are leaving people behind, so scout your route for curb cuts and working elevators. Designate 'slow zones' and make sure your marshals know to keep the pace steady for those with mobility aids or breathing issues. Always have a vehicle or a 'rest van' following the march so anyone who hits their limit can stay in the fight without hurting themselves.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: secure Document Sharing] Give me the short version: Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?

It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inclusivity in Action] A friend asked me: 'How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?' What do I tell them?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, phone Hygiene] What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Real talk: Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Here's the thing: Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Reaching the Unorganized] How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, community Gardens
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, community Gardens] The city says our neighborhood garden is illegal. Should we stop?

Keep planting and get the whole block to help you defend that dirt. Guerrilla gardening is an act of defiance against a system that wants us dependent on corporate grocery chains. If they try to bulldoze it, make sure there's a crowd there to stop them and a camera to record the state destroying a source of food. A plot of land that feeds people is more sacred than any zoning law written by a bureaucrat.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] Can you explain: how do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: Using Voter Files
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Using Voter Files] Do we really need expensive voter data software?

Data is just a map, but you're the one who has to walk the path. Use the basic public records to find out who hasn't been talked to in years—the renters, the young people, and the marginalized who the big parties ignore. Don't get bogged down in spreadsheets; use the information to target the doors where a conversation will have the most impact. Our strategy is to expand the electorate by engaging the people the system has abandoned.

title: Karl Organizing: Sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sliding Scales] Can you explain: how do we implement a sliding scale for events?

Real talk: Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: Spotting ICE
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Spotting ICE] Can you explain: what should I look for if I think ICE is in my neighborhood?

Let me break it down: Look for unmarked white or dark SUVs with tinted windows lurking near apartment complexes at dawn. They often wear vests that just say POLICE in generic block letters to trick folks into opening their doors. If you see them, blast the location to your network immediately with a photo of the plates. We protect our neighbors by being the early warning system the feds can't hide from.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: campaign Literature
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: campaign Literature] Give me the short version: What should my flyers look like?

Bold, clear, and high-contrast. No small print and no flowery language. Put your face on there so people know you're a neighbor, and list three concrete things you will do on Day One to make their lives easier. Use union printers and include the bug to show you support organized labor. Every flyer should have a clear call to action: join the fight, chip in to pool resources, or show up at the polls.

text:

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, enemy Counter-Fundraising] How do we use our opposition to raise money?

Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: mental Health Crisis
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: mental Health Crisis] Give me the short version: What do we do if a neighbor is having a mental health breakdown?

Calling 911 is a death sentence for people in crisis, so you need a team of neighbors trained in psychological first aid. Approach with empty hands, keep your voice low, and give the person plenty of physical space. Find out if they have a friend or a therapist they trust and get that person on the scene. Our goal is to bring them back to earth safely, not to restrain or terrorize them. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Marshals
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Marshals] What exactly are marshals supposed to do during the march?

Marshals are the backbone of our safety, keeping the crowd together and buffering us from traffic or hostile agitators. They are not cops; they don't boss comrades around, they facilitate the flow and watch the flanks for snatch squads. Give them high-vis vests and clear communication tools so they can spot trouble before it reaches the heart of our movement. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Work] I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?

Here's the thing: Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] Can you explain: what kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action.

title: Karl Organizing: Community defense network
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community defense network] How do I build a rapid response network?

Start with a Signal group of trusted neighbors. Define what triggers a response: ICE sighting, eviction attempt, police harassment. Assign roles: who verifies, who shows up, who documents, who calls lawyers. Drill it before you need it. A rapid response network that activates in 15 minutes saves lives.

title: Karl Organizing: Spotting ICE
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Spotting ICE] A friend asked me: 'What should I look for if I think ICE is in my neighborhood?' What do I tell them?

Look for unmarked white or dark SUVs with tinted windows lurking near apartment complexes at dawn. They often wear vests that just say POLICE in generic block letters to trick folks into opening their doors. If you see them, blast the location to your network immediately with a photo of the plates. We protect our neighbors by being the early warning system the feds can't hide from.

title: Karl Organizing: Time Bank Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Time Bank Value] A friend asked me: 'In a time bank, is an hour of plumbing worth more than an hour of childcare?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not. In our world, an hour of a human being's life is equal regardless of the task they're performing. The capitalists want us to believe some labor is 'unskilled' so they can pay us pennies, but we know better. Whether you're fixing a pipe or watching a comrade's kid so they can organize, you're contributing to our collective survival. We value the person, not the market price of their sweat.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: sustainer Programs] Give me the short version: Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Funds] What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

Look, You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, the Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, the Sheriff's Office] Is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?

Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable.
